CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  September 14, 2023
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  Lisa Massaro, Kim Luu, Katie Chan, Yvette Corona

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES
  Commission Members will vote to approve 5-11-23 and 7-13-23 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  UPDATE ITEMS
  a) Sustainability and Bike & Pedestrian Plans
  b) Turf Replacement Rebate
  c) Organics Waste Recycling Program
  d) Safe Clean Water Program
  e) Refill Store Opportunities
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  IV.  ALHAMBRA TREE ORDINANCE
  Commissioners will discuss their ideas on how to draft a stronger tree ordinance in order to save
  native trees and push to replace grass in front yards with California Native Plants.
  Recommended Action: Discussion item. No action required

  V.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please
  limit all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior
  to the meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business
  of the Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5)
  minutes.

  VI.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

  VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, January 11, 2024 at 6:00 p.m.

  1
9-14-23
 If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it to
the secretary. When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please
make your statement as brief as possible. The maximum time for addressing the Committee is five minutes.

If you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be
heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Committee on a subject
which does not appear on the agenda, but is of an environmental concern, your comments will be heard
under Public Comments. Please be advised that under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, the
Commission cannot take action on any item which does not appear on the agenda.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra
California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during regular business hours of
7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact David Dolphin, Deputy Director of Utilities, either in person at the
Utilities Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone at (626) 570-
5067 during regular business hours.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting of May 11, 2023

  The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
  order at 6:09 p.m. on May 11, 2023.

•  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Chan, Massaro, Corona

  Commission Members Absent: Luu

  Staff Present:  David Dolphin – Commission Secretary

  Members of the Public

  Lola Armendariz

•  VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES FROM 1/12/23
  Commissioner Chan motioned to approve the meeting minutes from 1/12/23.
  Commissioner Massaro seconded the motion. All Commissioners present voted in
  favor to approve the minutes. Motion to approve passed.

  Commission Chan prepared to chair the meeting and review the agenda items.

•  UPDATE ITEMS
  Provided in the Agenda packets, verbally provided by the City as follows:

  A.  Sustainability and Bike & Pedestrian Plans
  • On April 10, 2023, the Sustainability Plan was awarded for
  contract to Environmental Science Associates (ESA). Contract
  execution is currently underway. The plan itself is expected to
  take as much as 26 months to complete. We will know more once
  our kick off meeting between staff and the consultant takes place
  over the next couple of weeks.
  • Bike and Pedestrian Consultants (Alta Planning) are currently
  going through data analysis based on their early inventory,
  research, and survey work. They are on pace to complete the draft
  by the Fall. At that point, staff will review the draft and work with
  the Consultant towards public outreach and intake before Council
  adoption.

  Page 1 of 7
   ITEM #2

B.  Turf Replacement Rebate
  The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) has
  submitted the application for the DWR Drought Relief Grant to provide
  assistance to its member agencies to fund a turf replacement rebate
  program. Alhambra is a member agency.

C.  Organic Waste Recycling Program
  • The City has been working with Republic Services on fully
  meeting the organics diversion requirements of SB 1383 and
  AB 1826 through site visits and waste assessments. Every
  single-family residence, multifamily complex, and commercial
  business should have organic waste collection services. If they
  do not, they should contact Republic Services at
  alhambra@republicservices.com.
  • The Community Garden will be introducing organic waste
  collection. Outreach material and information explaining the
  changes will be posted and provided to all community garden
  patrons.
  • The City is working with a marketing firm to create a social
  media ad campaign, a new organics webpage, and an
  interactive game on sorting with the goal of increasing
  diversion. Material will be published as they are created.
  • The Spring Alhambra Recycles Event held on Saturday, April
  22nd was a great success. Residents expressed gratitude and
  interest in recycling, composting and keeping Alhambra clean.
  The statistics for the event:
  • Total car tally: 363
  • Document shredding participants: 168
  • Electronic waste disposal participants: 195
  • Compost giveaway participants: 106 (10 tons of compost
  distributed)
  • Our next Alhambra Recycles Event will be held in the Fall.
  Until then, the recycling assistant and Republic Services are
  programming environmental and sustainability-focused camp
  activities for Camp Alhambra this Summer. They are also
  working on developing more outreach events to educate and
  inform residents on the importance and correct ways to
  compost and recycle at home. More information will be posted
  on the City’s website and social media.

D.  Safe Clean Water Program (SCWP)
  The City has submitted an application for funding the following
  stormwater capture projects:

  Page 2 of 7
   ITEM #2
  •  Burke Heritage Park and Marengo Yard – The project was
  approved for full funding. We anticipate an RFP for design to be
  released in 7/2023.
  •  Green Street Demonstration Project on Main St – This project was
  not approved for funding through the SCWP; however, the project
  awarded funding through the Urban Greening Grant, California
  Natural Resources Agency ($3M). We plan to submit an
  application through the SCWP for FY 24-25 for construction costs.

  Fact sheets included in Agenda Packet

  E.  Eco Fair 2023

  The City of Alhambra had its annual Eco Fair on Sunday, April 23, 2023.
  This event was attended by many residents and Council Members. Several
  vendors provided information regarding tools, resources, and samples to
  the community to encourage recycling, reusing materials where possible,
  and reducing their overall contribution to the waste stream. City staff
  distributed approximately 760 water conservation and stormwater
  pollution prevention items to attendees.
  It was a successful event with many activities for the children.

  Commissioner Chan asked for more detail on how the consultant will work toward
  public outreach and intake for the Sustainability and Bike & Pedestrian Plan. She
  noted there were concerns from residents at the last meeting. Commissioner Chang
  also wanted to know the turnaround time for the turf replacement grant. Staff advised
  information will be provided after contacting the proper staff at the City Manager’s
  office and the turnaround time for the Turf Replacement Grant Varies depending on
  the State. The rebate will be an additional rebate as the City does not have a rebate
  for turf replacement currently.

  Commissioner Chan would like to have advertising for composting in paper form
  since a lot of people are not technologically savvy. Staff advised there is a Recycling
  Specialist that handles the advertising. The social media campaign would be in
  addition to the current hard copy advertising. Also, include interactive gaming.

  Commissioner Corona stated the information was confusing when it was first sent
  out. Republic sent out mixed messaging and it needs to be corrected.
  Communication should be effectively sent to residents in regards to what should be
  placed in each bin.

•  STORMWATER 101 PRESENTATION

  David Dolphin, Deputy Director of Utilities for the City of Alhambra, presented
  information to the Environmental Sustainability Commission regarding stormwater
  regulations and the challenges to prevent pollutant discharges. The presentation also

  Page 3 of 7
   ITEM #2
  gave the Commissioners a brief overview of the City’s storm drain system and
  techniques to prevent pollutant discharges.

  Staff advised the Commission of the purpose of the presentation which was for
  information only. Also, stormwater pollution information is available on the City’s
  website. No action needed.

  Commissioner Corona disagreed with rain down the drain and stated the water should
  go back to the water table when possible. Ideally, water should be captured before it
  enters the ocean. Also, we need to plant more California Native Plants. Staff advised
  the storm drain system was built to prevent flooding and most of the stormwater in
  Alhambra discharges to the Rio Hondo during a rain event. The Rio Hondo has
  spreading grounds to capture the stormwater in order to infiltrate to groundwater.

  Staff advised the Commission of the Safe Clean Water Program and the goals of
  Measure W to fund projects to capture stormwater and improve water quality.

  Commissioner Massaro mentioned rain gardens as a great resource which utilized
  rain barrels and would like to discuss as an agenda item at the next meeting.

  Commissioner Corona mentioned a great resource, Harvesting Rainwater, a book that
  explains how to harvest rainwater at your home.

  Commissioner Chan mentioned the Friends of the LA River whose goal is to return
  the LA River to the natural state.

  Staff gave a review of the Brown Act and the requirements of the agenda.

•  ALHAMBRA TREE ORDINANCE

  Commissioner Chan would like to adopt a stronger tree ordinance and provide
  resources to residents to educate them on the importance of trees and provide
  locations for small businesses to purchase California Native Plants which correlates
  with the move to remove grass from our front yard.

  Commissioners reviewed the documents presented in the Agenda Packet. In
  summary, The City of Alhambra, Monterey Park and Rosemead are the only local
  cites without current preservation ordinance for trees on private property. The current
  regulations only cover City owned trees on City property.

  Commissioner Chan stated many of the neighboring cities such as the City of LA and
  LA County have protections for oak tree preservation as well as different species.
  Many of them offer protection for mature trees on public and private property.
  Commission Chan mentioned the following items from the Alhambra Tree Ordinance
  that were alarming and need attention:
  • trees that are removed must be replaced based on the diameter of the trunk
  removed, e.g., if a 60” tree is removed it cannot be replaced by a 61” tree.

  Page 4 of 7
   ITEM #2
  •  Only accept four tree replacements for one tree removed.
  •  If they remove trees 50% can be replaced by new pavement.
  •  Removing oak trees and native species- entire section is questionable.
  •  Director of Development Services makes the final decision. If the public
  disagree, they can appeal to the Planning Commission.
  •  Appeal process should be modified to include the Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.

  All Commissioners agreed with Commissioner Chan’s suggestion to go over the entire
  ordinance and bring up the parts that are vague and not acceptable and present the
  findings to the Council Members.

  Commissioner Massaro -An Organics Recycling event at Rose Bowl had a lot of turf
  and oak trees that were diseased. The machinery that comes to remove the tree starts
  the process of polluting the air which caused the demise of the trees in the first place.
  During the event she learned a lot about fertilizing.

  Commissioner Corona – When trees are removed the carbon in the soil gets burned up
  and it is unfortunate because oak trees are a keystone species. The provide life for
  everyone including humans and they host 250 plus caterpillars that feed birds. When
  we cut down oak tree, we lose the diversity around the trees.

  Commissioner Chan- propose to amend the ordinance is to change the required
  percentage of planting California Native plants to 100 percent and provide the
  resources to residents.

  Suggest we review the feedback on how the Commission will envision the new
  ordinance and put place it on the next agenda to see what we want to add or change. It
  will be a discussion item on the next agenda. Council members will be urged to
  review it and vote on it.

•  CLOSED LOOP SUSTAINABLE COMPOST

  Commissioner Chan- Proposes to have a compost bin at the Alhambra Farmer’s
  Market for drop off and keep within the City of Alhambra possibly the Alhambra
  Community Garden. Residents can provide compostable material and in return pick
  up compost throughout the year instead of an annual event.

  Staff advised the City has a plan to have the Community Gardens as a compost site.

  Commissioner Corona- LA Compost should be invited as their organization has set
  up stations within other Community Gardens. Our goal is to make sure the compost
  remains available to the Alhambra community.

•  COOP AND REFILL STORES

  Page 5 of 7
   ITEM #2
  Commissioner Chan- A COOP is a community-based organization or business that is
  community run. A refill store is where you bring your own bag and fill them with
  market items; such as nuts, gummy bears, similar to the front of Sprouts.
  There are refill stores that are currently open in the City of LA and it would be
  beneficial to have one closer in the San Gabriel Valley.
  Commissioners agreed it would be beneficial to the community to have a refill store
  located in Alhambra.

  Staff will check to see if there are grant opportunities for refill stores in the City of
  Alhambra.

•  PUBLIC COMMENT

  Received 3 speaker request cards from Lola Armendariz.

  Ms. Armendariz requested additional public comment period which was agreed upon
  by Commissioner Chan. Staff made clarifications on the purpose of the Comment
  Period as it relates to the Brown Act.

  Bike Pedestrian Plan. Proposed route is unknown and would like to get more
  information. Requested information from the Council.

  Stormwater Presentation- Item #4 – Expressed concern about Burke Park and water
  storage and the ramifications of construction.  The City must provide proper
  notification to residents.

  Alhambra Tree Ordinance – Item #5 – Concerned about removing grass and replacing
  with native plants and the condition of trees in Alhambra.

  Turf Replacement Plan – Leaf blowers should not be used when there are vacuums
  available. They are creating pollution. Trees on Alhambra Road from Atlantic to
  Huntington are dying. The City needs to check the trees.

  Commission Chan moved to end Public Comment.

•  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  Items on the next agenda Rain gardens and water cycle; tree ordinance; farmers
  market composting an update item and/or community events.

  Commissioner Corona- Need to educate the community on importance of native
  plants and what they provide and the difference between the two since we are
  discussing turf replacement and the tree ordinance. If you have someone to speak
  about the topic of rain gardens, we should invite them as a guest speaker.

  Page 6 of 7
   ITEM #2
•  ADJOURNMENT

  Commissioner Chan motioned to adjourn the meeting at 7:42 PM, Commissioner
  Massaro seconded. Motion unanimously approved.

  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting of July 13, 2023

  The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
  order at 6:02 p.m. on July 13, 2023.

•  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Chan, Corona

  Commission Members Absent: Luu, Massaro

  Staff Present:  David Dolphin – Commission Secretary

  We did not have a quorum.

•  ADJOURNMENT

  Commissioner Chan motioned to adjourn the meeting at 6:04 PM, Due to a lack of
  quorum.

Environmental Sustainability Commission Meeting- September 14, 2023
Update Items

  1. Sustainability and Bike & Pedestrian Plans
  • Consultants and City staff continue to gather data in relation to examining
  environmental sustainability opportunities in Alhambra. As part of the process, the
  development of the City’s plan will also include stakeholder outreach and community
  engagement to better understand the community’s needs and concerns. The schedule
  for such outreach is anticipated for the Fall of 2023.

  Meanwhile, staff attended the California Adaptation Forum, featuring much discussion
  about sustainability and climate adaptation. These are important opportunities to learn
  from environmental experts and practices from other jurisdictions. Heat mitigation was
  at the center of many conversations.

  •  The development of the Bike and Pedestrian Plan draft continues, with release of the
  plan for public review tentatively in the Fall of 2023. Alta Planning and staff continue to
  evaluate bike and ped improvement concepts, network, and locations. In July 2023,
  staff worked with the consultant to identify some bike and pedestrian improvement
  opportunities along the south end of the City for the purposes of qualifying for the
  Metro Express Lanes Round 3 Net Toll Revenue Reinvestment Grant Program.
  Authorization to apply was submitted to the City Council at the July 24, 2023 meeting.
  Details of the City’s improvement are identified in the staff report. In summary, the
  grant request includes bike and ped improvements at Poplar Boulevard and Palm
  Avenue; Marguerita Avenue; Corto Street and Almansor Street; Chapel Avenue; South
  Alhambra Greenway; and Alhambra Road. The majority of the work is for “quick build”
  to enable quick and affordable installation and to further engage the community before
  permanent changes are installed. If awarded, the grants funds will be announced in
  October 2023.

  2. Turf Replacement Rebate

  The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) has submitted the application for
  the DWR Drought Relief Grant to provide assistance to its member agencies to fund a turf
  replacement rebate program. There has been no movement from the state since our last
  meeting.

  3. Organic Waste Recycling Program
  • The City hosted two Organics Recycling Workshops for Alhambra residents on 8.23.2023
  at Reese Hall. Participants learned the importance of organics recycling, how to separate
  their waste properly, tips to maintain cleanliness of their containers, and additional
  programs offered to residents by Republic Services. Residents that were unable to
  attend are encouraged to access resources on bit.ly/alhambrarecycles. The City plans to
  have another workshop in the Winter.
   ITEM #3

  •  LA County hosted a Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) Collection Event on 8.26.2023
  at their LA Public Works Headquarters building in Alhambra. Residents that missed this
  event are encouraged to visit https://www.cityofalhambra.org/667/Household-
  Hazardous-Waste and utilize the City of Los Angeles’ HHW permanent collection sites,
  which are available for free to all LA County residents year-round.
  •  New resources to increase participation in the City’s organics recycling program through
  behavior change, including a “Compost Charlie Recycling Game,” are available to
  residents at bit.ly/alhambrarecycles. Additional resources and content to come soon.
  •  The City is hosting a Compost Giveaway Event on 9.30.2023 from 9AM to 12PM at
  Granada Park. Please note that unlike previous years, compost giveaway service is a
  separate event from our Alhambra Recycles Event. Be sure to bring your own container.
  More information at bit.ly/alhambrarecycles. Flyer included in Agenda Packet
  •  The City is hosting their bi-annual Alhambra Recycles Event on 10.7.2023 from 8AM to
  12PM at Granada Park. Residents are able to recycle electronic waste, plastic bottles,
  and aluminum cans, and shred documents on-site. Compost will be given away at a
  separate event on 9.30.2023. First 175 participants will receive a free Fosselman’s Ice
  Cream scoop voucher. More information at bit.ly/alhambrarecycles.
  Flyer included in Agenda Packet
  •  The City and Republic Services are hosting an Organics Recycling Workshop for
  Alhambra businesses on 11.16.2023. Businesses will learn about new requirements for
  organics recycling and food recovery and exchange tips on best practices. More
  information to come.

4. Safe Clean Water Program (SCWP)

  The City has submitted an application for funding the following stormwater capture projects:
  • Green Street Demonstration Project on Main St – Application was submitted to the
  Safe Clean Water Program FY 2024-25 call for projects by the deadline, July 31, 2023.
  We are seeking funding for construction and operations & maintenance costs.
  • A Request for Proposals for design was released on 7/27/23. A total of 3 proposals were
  received and are currently under review.

5. Refill Stores

  The City of Alhambra Grant Specialist is not aware of any grant opportunities that are available
  for Refill Stores. One of the reasons could be these markets are privately owned and for profit.

  The City of Alhambra’s Economic Development Specialist did not receive inquiries from anyone
  expressing interest in opening a refill store. The City would welcome these establishments and
  will keep an eye open for opportunities. Contact Tiffany Chew, Economic Development
  Specialist, 626-570-5038 if you know of anyone interested in opening a refill store in Alhambra.

  CHAPTER 23.88: TREE PRESERVATION

§ 23.88.010 PURPOSE AND SCOPE.

  (A) Intent and purpose. This Chapter is established to recognize oaks, and other California native and mature trees as
significant aesthetic and ecological resources and to create favorable conditions for the preservation and propagation of
plant heritage for the benefit of the current and future residents of the city. It is the intent of this chapter to maintain and
enhance the public health, safety and welfare through the mitigation of soil erosion and air pollution. It is also the intent of
this chapter to preserve and enhance property values through conserving and enhancing the distinctive and unique
aesthetic character of many areas in the city.
 (B) Scope.
  (1) No protected trees as herein defined shall be removed or damaged except in conformance with the provisions of
this chapter. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all protected trees on all private property in all zoning districts,
except in the rear and side yards of single family residential dwellings of R-1 and R-2 zoning districts, whether vacant,
undeveloped, in the process of development or developed. Protected trees shall not be topped or trimmed except as
allowed in the exceptions in division (B)(2) below. Pruning shall not be subject to a tree permit unless, in the opinion of the
Community Development Director or designee, the work is so extensive as to constitute trimming, topping, or otherwise
damage the tree.
  (2) Exceptions. The following are exempt from the provisions of this chapter:
  (a) Combined permit. A separate tree permit is not required when a tree removal is requested as part of an
entitlement application. However, all other provisions of this chapter apply and must be considered by the Planning
Commission as part of the combined development permit.
  (b) Emergency situation. Cases of emergency where the Community Development Director or the Director of Public
Works or their designees, or any member of a law enforcement agency or Fire Department, in the performance of his or her
duties, determines that protected tree poses an imminent threat to the public safety, or general welfare.
  (c) Visual barriers. Removal or relocation of protected trees necessary to obtain adequate line-of-sight distances for
traffic safety as required by the Community Development Director or the Director of Public Works Services or their
designees.
  (d) Public property and public utilities. Removal or trimming of trees for the protection of any public property or public
utility property that is undertaken by authority of the city, any other public agency having jurisdiction, or any public utility.
  (e) Routine trimming. Normal and routine trimming or pruning which does not result in damage or death to a tree.
Removal of deadwood is allowed without a permit.
  (f) Fruit trees. Any fruit tree may be trimmed or removed without a permit.
  (g) Palm trees. Any palm tree, except as listed as California native, may be trimmed or removed without a permit.
(Ord. 4737, passed 7-23-18)
§ 23.88.020 DEFINITIONS.

 (A) General. This section provides definitions of the technical and other terms and phrases used in
this chapter as a means of providing consistency in its interpretation. Where any definition in this section may conflict with
definitions in other titles of the Alhambra Municipal Code, these definitions shall prevail for the purposes of this Code. If a
word is not defined in this section or in other provisions of the Municipal Code, the most common dictionary definition is
presumed to be correct.

  DAMAGE. Any action undertaken which causes injury, death, or disfigurement to a protected tree. This includes, but is
not limited to, cutting, poisoning, overwatering, topping, trimming, relocating or transplanting a protected tree.
  DEVELOPMENT PERMIT. An application to use, alter, construct upon, or otherwise change the use of land or a
structure.
  MULTI-TRUNK. Any tree with multiple trunks attributed to a single tree. For purposes of determining the diameter of a
multi-trunk tree, the diameter of each trunk shall be measured at a point four and one-half feet above the root crown, and the
sum of the diameters shall be the diameter of the tree.
  PROTECTED TREES. Includes the following:
  (a) Quercus family trees (oaks) and California native trees taller than 15 feet, or with a trunk diameter larger than 12
inches in diameter, or 36 inches in circumference, measured at a point four and one-half feet above the root crown.
  (b) Mature tree: A tree taller than 20 feet or with a trunk diameter larger 24 inches in diameter, or 75 inches in
circumference, measured at a point four and one-half feet above the root crown.
  PRUNING (also known as LACING). The removal of selected branches that are dead, a hazard to public or property, or
are otherwise selected for removal while preserving the overall form of the tree. Pruning can be done to give a tree a more
balanced appearance, to reduce the weight on one side of a tree in order to prevent the tree from toppling, or to remove
branches that are at risk of breaking and injuring people or damaging property. Utilities may use pruning to selectively
remove branches that interfere with overhead lines. PRUNING is distinct from topping or trimming a tree.
  REMOVAL. The uprooting, cutting, or severing of the main trunk, of a protected tree.
  ROOT CROWN. That portion of a protected tree trunk from which roots extend laterally into the ground.
  TOPPING. The removal of the uppermost branches of a tree, or cutting the trunk, in order to reduce its height without
regard to the overall form of the tree. Typically results in a horizontal cut across the trunk or a roughly spherical cut centered
on the trunk.
  TRIMMING. The alteration of the outward shape of a tree without regard to which branches are to be trimmed. Typically
results in a geometric rather than natural shape. Hedges are trimmed to preserve a particular, frequently rectangular, shape.
Topping a tree would be an extreme example of TRIMMING.
  UNDEVELOPED PROPERTY. Land which is in its natural, original, or pristine state.
  VACANT PROPERTY. Land on which no buildings or improvements have been erected or orchards planted but which
may have been graded for drainage or other purposes.
(Ord. 4737, passed 7-23-18)
§ 23.08.030 PERMITS AND REQUIRED PROTECTIVE MEASURES.

  (A) Tree permit required. A tree permit shall be obtained prior to the removal of any protected tree except as allowed in
the exceptions in § 23.88.010(B).
 (B) Application and fees.
  (1) Tree permit for the removal of a protected tree that is diseased and/or damaged by storm, fire or other natural
disaster or otherwise determined to be dangerous by the City Manager, Community Development Director, police officer,
firefighter or Code Enforcement Officer.
  (a) An application for a tree permit for the removal of a diseased or hazardous protected tree shall be made to the
Community Development Department.
  (b) There is no fee for a tree permit for the removal of a diseased or hazardous protected tree; however, the applicant
must submit documentation supporting the condition of the tree to the Community Development Department, as deemed
necessary by the Director.
  (2) Tree permit for the removal of healthy protected trees.
  (a) An application for a tree permit for the removal of a healthy protected tree shall be made to the Community
Development Department. The content, form, instructions, procedures, and requirements of the application package
deemed necessary and appropriate for the proper enforcement of this chapter shall be established by the Community
Development Department. The application shall include, but not be limited to the following:
  (b) An explanation as to why the tree’s removal is necessary.
  (c) An explanation as to why tree removal is more desirable than alternative project designs.
  (d) An explanation of any mitigation measures.
   (e) A fee per the city’s fee schedule.
 (C) Action on application.
  (1) Tree permit for the removal of diseased and hazardous protected trees.
  (a) Upon the receipt of an application to remove a diseased or hazardous protected tree, the Director or his or her
designee shall have ten working days to approve, conditionally approve, or deny the application.
  (b) If the Director or his or her designee denies such application, the decision may be appealed to the Planning
Commission. Such appeal shall be processed pursuant to the appeal regulations. The fee for an appeal shall be the same as
for an appeal of a Design Review Board decision.
  (c) The privileges granted an applicant in this section shall become null and void if not utilized within six months from
the date of the approval.
  (2) Tree permit for the removal of healthy protected trees.
  (a) The application for a tree permit for the removal of a healthy protected tree or trees shall be subject to the
approval, conditional approval, or denial of the Director or his or her designee or the Planning Commission (on appeal) or
City Council (on appeal).
  (b) Notice shall be provided in compliance with Alhambra Municipal Code (Public Notices and Hearings) and shall be
mailed to all owners of real property as shown on the latest assessment rolls of the city or of the county, located within a
radius of 300 feet of the exterior boundaries of the parcel that is the subject of the hearing; and any other person whose
property may, in the judgment of the Director, be affected by the proposed project at least 14 days before the date of the
Director’s consideration and final decision as stated in the notice.
  The mailed notice shall state that the Director will consider and decide whether to approve, conditionally approve, or
deny the removal of a healthy protected tree application on a dated specified in the notice.
  The Director may defer action and refer the request to the planning Commission for consideration and final decision.
  (c) The privileges granted an applicant in this section shall become null and void if not utilized within one year from
the date of the approval or conditional approval.
 (D) Replacement tree conditions.
  (1) Replacement tree conditions for the removal of diseased and/or hazardous protected trees.No replacement tree
shall be required.
  (2) Replacement tree conditions for the removal of healthy protected trees.
  (a) Quercus family (oaks) and California native trees: Two 24-inch box replacement oak or native trees shall be
required for each ten-inch increment of the diameter of the existing tree, or portion thereof.
  (b) Mature trees: One 24-inch box replacement similar or native trees shall be required for each ten-inch increment of
the diameter of the existing tree, or portion thereof.
  (c) The following options shall apply to the total number of required replacement trees:
  A. A minimum of 50% replacement trees shall be planted on site. The remaining balance of required replacement
trees may be planted off-site at locations approved by the Director.
  B. A maximum of 50% required replacement trees may be substituted with an in-lieu fee payment. The value of
each replacement tree, including the cost of installation, shall be established by a certified arborist and the funds shall be
dedicated to an urban forestry program of the City of Alhambra.
(Ord. 4737, passed 7-23-18)
§ 23.88.040 ENFORCEMENT AND LIABILITY.

 (A) Enforcement.
  (1) The Community Development Department will monitor construction activities for compliance with the provisions of
this chapter.
  (2) Whenever a tree removal has occurred in conjunction with construction or work contrary to the provisions of this
chapter, a Code Enforcement Officer shall issue a citation per tree removed without a permit and a city inspector shall issue
a notice to the responsible party to “stop work” on the project on which the violation has occurred. No work shall be allowed
until the citation has been paid and the violation has been rectified and approved by the Director.
  (3) Whenever a tree removal has occurred, independent of a development project, contrary to the provision of this
chapter, no building permits on the property associated with the violation shall be issued for a period of one year.
  (4) Whenever a tree removal has occurred contrary to the provision of this chapter, the required number of replacement
trees shall be double the standard provision.
 (Ord. 4737, passed 7-23-18)
